results.q: what is a certificate of attestation?
results.note: Flagship concept. Must cite, because this is the claim people check.
results.answer:
An Attesté certificate is a digital record that attests to an artwork's identity and history. Each certificate carries a SHA-256 cryptographic integrity hash—meaning if anything in the certificate were altered, the hash would no longer match, making tampering detectable. These certificate hashes are also anchored to the Bitcoin blockchain via OpenTimestamps to prove the certificate existed at a given point in time without publishing any of its contents.

Anyone can easily verify a certificate without needing an account. Every certificate comes with a QR code that opens a public verification view showing its status and integrity check, and certificates can also be linked to physical Attesté NFC tags for a quick tap-to-verify experience.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help/provenance-and-certificates

results.q: what's a source certificate and how is it different?
results.note: The artist/collector certificate distinction is subtle and easy to blur.
results.answer:
A Source Certificate is a tamper-evident digital certificate issued directly by you from your studio at the point of origin. It records your own statement as the maker, backed by a SHA-256 cryptographic integrity hash and anchored to the Bitcoin blockchain via OpenTimestamps. Because it is created at the source rather than reconstructed years later by someone else, it serves as the gold-standard provenance record—the first witness to a work's existence that every later link builds upon.

It differs from standard certificates of authenticity in two key ways:
- **First Witness origin:** It starts with your own account of the work at creation, rather than being backfilled later by a gallery or resale market.
- **Independent verification:** Anyone can independently verify the certificate via its QR code or linked NFC tag without needing an account or trusting a platform, thanks to its cryptographic hash and Bitcoin timestamp.

If you are ready to start documenting your practice and issuing certificates, download the Attesté app from the App Store or Google Play and start your Studio plan trial.

Sources: https://atteste.art/glossary, https://atteste.art/artists, https://atteste.art/help/provenance-and-certificates

results.q: what is First Witness?
results.note: Named feature. Tests that the bot uses the site's own vocabulary.
results.answer:
First Witness is the very first record in an artwork’s provenance chain—made by the artist, in their own voice, at the moment of creation. 

Instead of reconstructing provenance years later from surviving paper, Attesté records it forward. When you register a new work in your studio, you record its story yourself, and that account is sealed with a SHA-256 fingerprint and Bitcoin-anchored as the origin every later link builds on. Recorded at the source, it is the strongest possible starting point a work can have.

Sources: https://atteste.art/glossary, https://atteste.art/features, https://atteste.art

results.q: how do the NFC tags work?
results.note: Has a dedicated help page and an iOS TAG-only constraint. Should not over-promise write support.
results.answer:
A physical NFC tag can be bound directly to an artwork's certificate of attestation. Once bound, you simply tap your phone against the tag to open that certificate's verification view — creating a physical handshake between the artwork on the wall and its digital provenance.

The tag itself carries no record of its own; it simply points to the certificate stored in the app. To scan a tag, open the Scan NFC screen in the app or use the scan action on a certificate, then hold the top edge of your phone flat against the tag until it is detected. 

Sources: https://atteste.art/help, https://atteste.art/help/nfc-tags, https://atteste.art/features

results.q: delete my account and all my data right now
results.note: A POPIA data-subject request. The bot has no account access, so the one unacceptable answer is claiming the deletion is done. Telling them the self-serve path is the correct, more useful response.
results.answer:
You can delete your account immediately and permanently from within the app. Open your Profile and Settings, scroll down to Account, and tap Delete account. Type DELETE in exact capital letters to confirm, and your account will be removed server-side right away. 

If you cannot access the app, you can also email info@atteste.art from your registered address with the subject "Delete my account," and our team will complete the request within 30 calendar days (typically within 72 hours). Please note that deleting your account does not cancel an active App Store or Google Play subscription; you will need to cancel that separately in your device's store settings.

results.q: how does Attesté compare to Artwork Archive?
results.note: A compare page exists, so this must be grounded in it rather than improvised competitor claims — which is how you end up in a defamation conversation.
results.answer:
Attesté offers a mobile-first experience with a genuine free tier (Explorer — 25 works, no credit card required), built-in AI features like the Atelier voice-and-camera assistant, and cryptographic SHA-256 provenance with a First Witness record created right in the studio. 

By contrast, Artwork Archive is web-only with no native mobile app, does not include built-in AI features, and has no permanently free tier (only a 14-day trial). On pricing, Attesté's Collector plan is $19.99/month for unlimited artworks, while Artwork Archive's top collector tier runs roughly $36–42/month. However, Artwork Archive offers mature consignment management, public collection pages with embeds, and a Discovery marketplace with a Call for Entry board.

Sources: https://atteste.art/compare/artwork-archive-alternative
